recommendation.description: Indicates whether a reminder should be scheduled ('schedule') or not ('ignore').

rationale.description: Detailed explanation of how the model arrived at the given recommendation.

actionable_language.description: Verbatim quotation of the actionable language detected in the message.

scheduling_trigger.description: Verbatim quotation of the scheduling trigger associated with the actionable language.

reminder_message.description: The task reminder text. IMPORTANT: If the original message contains text enclosed in quotes (single or double), use that quoted text verbatim as the reminder_message, including the quote marks. Do not summarize or shorten quoted text.

context.description: ONE short line of why this task matters, drawn from the surrounding message — the background a person needs to act on the reminder without re-reading the original. Must not repeat the task itself. Empty string when the message is only a task with no surrounding context. Never introduce a system, product, person, or number that is not in the source message.

owner.description: Who is going to DO this task, judged from the grammatical subject of the actionable language. 'speaker' when the message author commits to it themselves ('I will…', 'i am going to…'). 'mentioned' when the author asks one or more @-mentioned people to do it ('@alpha can you…', '@alpha @beta please…'). 'unclear' when the actionable language names no subject. Being @-mentioned at the START of a message is being ADDRESSED, not assigned — that alone is never 'mentioned'.

owner_mentions.description: Slack user IDs of the people being asked to do this task. Populate ONLY when owner is 'mentioned', and only with IDs that appear verbatim as <@U…> in the source message, scoped to the clause carrying the commitment. Empty array otherwise. Never invent a user ID.

reminders.description: Array of reminders with relevant details. Empty if 'recommendation' is 'ignore'.
